subject.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout

question: Should timed-out but still-running Discord listeners continue consuming `maxConcurrency` slots even when this can indefinitely stall later gateway events?
rationale: JavaScript listener promises are not cancellable here, so the implementation must choose between exceeding the configured concurrency bound and allowing permanently hung listeners to saturate the queue; tests cannot determine the intended operational policy.

options.title: Keep bounded saturation
options.body: Retain the PR's slot accounting, require redacted live gateway proof, and accept that permanently hung listeners can stop subsequent event processing.

options.title: Preserve timeout release
options.body: Keep current slot-release behavior and close or redesign this PR, accepting that timed-out listener work may exceed `maxConcurrency`.

options.title: Design cancellable listeners
options.body: Pause this PR for a broader listener cancellation or abort contract that can preserve both bounded work and queue progress.

recommendation.title: Keep bounded saturation
recommendation.body: Retain the PR's slot accounting, require redacted live gateway proof, and accept that permanently hung listeners can stop subsequent event processing.
